detail:
Decisions: Chose to read the live board from twining.db directly (read-only open) with fallback order db -> records/posts -> blackboard.jsonl, replacing the v1/v2 order that preferred blackboard.jsonl whenever it was non-empty — on a sqlite backend the JSONL is a pre-migration leftover that stops tracking the database, so the probe was measuring a board that had not existed for months; verified on the dogfood store where the stale file claimed 3 warnings and 162 statuses while the database held 15 warnings, 6 needs and zero statuses; Chose to print the resolved live-board source in the probe header ('live board from: twining.db') rather than only recording it in the JSON — the failure mode was silent for two versions and a visible source line makes a wrong-source reading self-evident in the console output someone pastes back; Chose to filter archiver-loop junk out of H2/H2b using the same conservative six-field signature as src/engine/archive-compactor.ts, and surface the count separately as H2c, rather than dropping the archive hypotheses — the junk is machine exhaust from the fixed #35 feedback loop, so counting it as destroyed tacit knowledge overstated H2b by roughly three orders of magnitude, but real findings ARE still swept hours old on clean post-fix sweeps; Chose to keep every pre-registered threshold untouched while fixing the instrument twice — H1 stays REFUTES at 13.6% against a 15% threshold despite being 3.4x the dogfood rate, because moving a threshold after seeing the number would destroy the falsifiability the whole exercise depends on
Findings: WITHDRAWN: I raised a suspected broken archive-exemption for unresolved warnings/needs, inferred from a field live board showing zero of both. That reading came entirely from the stale blackboard.jsonl. Corrected on the dogfood store: 15 warnings and 6 needs sit live, the exemption works, and H3 evaluates to REFUTES with 0 resolved-but-live of 21 obligations. Do not chase this.; Field results that survived both instrument corrections because they are decision-derived (records/decisions matches the decisions table exactly, 400/400): H1b at 92.1% (1100 placeholder + 365 fragment of 1226 decisions with alternatives) and H5 at 14.1% surfaced in the busiest scope (analysis/ holds 262 decisions, ~37 fit a 4000-token budget; 5 scopes over budget). Both are bug-shaped, not architecture-shaped.; Field REFUTES H4 at 3.7% project-scoped (predicted >=20%) and H7 at 9.3% assembled_before:false (predicted >=30%). Scope discipline in the field repo is excellent (analysis/, specs/claim-machinery/, specs/governance-kernel/) and Gate 1 compliance is good. Both concerns should be dropped from the structural plan.; warning: The review's archive recommendation was wrong as written. I proposed replacing the archiver's cutoff=now default with an age-based cutoff; against the #35 loop generating ~400k findings/day that would have exploded the live board. Aggressive archiving was the immune response. Only the count-based form (retain newest K) is safe, which is what the adversarial verifier originally specified.; The field repo carries unrepaired #35 damage: 9,141,126 archive entries, one 2026-07-08 sweep alone holding 328,657. Remedy is twining_housekeeping({compact_archives: true}) — preview then execute; likely reclaims GBs.; Instrument lesson: two of the five board-derived hypotheses were wrong for two versions and nothing in the output revealed it. A probe that reports a derived measurement should also report which source it derived it from, or a silent wrong-source read looks identical to a real result.
summary: Probe v2/v3: excluded archive-loop junk, then fixed live-board source after Dave caught the instrument reporting zero warnings a dashboard was showing
